papers.title: Nanostructured Pluronic hydrogels as bioinks for 3D bioprinting
papers.abstract: Bioprinting is an emerging technology in the field of tissue engineering as it allows the precise positioning of biologically relevant materials in 3D, which more resembles the native tissue in our body than current homogenous, bulk approaches. There is however a lack of materials to be used with this technology and materials such as the block copolymer Pluronic have good printing properties but do not allow long-term cell culture. Here we present an approach called nanostructuring to increase the biocompatibility of Pluronic gels at printable concentrations. By mixing acrylated with unmodified Pluronic F127 it was possible to maintain the excellent printing properties of Pluronic and to create stable gels via UV crosslinking. By subsequent elution of the unmodified Pluronic from the crosslinked network we were able to increase the cell viability of encapsulated chondrocytes at day 14 from 62% for a pure acrylated Pluronic hydrogel to 86% for a nanostructured hydrogel. The mixed Pluronic gels also showed good printability when cells where included in the bioink. The nanostructured gels were, with a compressive modulus of 1.42 kPa, mechanically weak, but we were able to increase the mechanical properties by the addition of methacrylated hyaluronic acid. Our nanostructuring approach enables Pluronic hydrogels to have the desired set of properties in all stages of the bioprinting process.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及生物打印中的生物墨水开发，但未使用任何人工智能或机器学习方法，与AI驱动生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate any AI/ML methods, lacks experimental validation using AI, and does not advance from observation to autonomous decision-making in bioprinting.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发适合生物打印且支持长期细胞培养的Pluronic水凝胶
summary_zh.method: 混合丙烯酸化和未改性Pluronic F127，UV交联后洗脱未改性部分形成纳米结构
summary_zh.result: 纳米结构水凝胶在14天时细胞活力从62%提升至86%
summary_zh.validation: 通过细胞活力测试和压缩模量测量验证

summary_en.motivation: To develop Pluronic hydrogels with improved biocompatibility for long-term cell culture in 3D bioprinting.
summary_en.method: Nanostructuring by mixing acrylated and unmodified Pluronic F127 followed by UV crosslinking and elution to enhance cell viability.
summary_en.result: Nanostructured hydrogels increased chondrocyte viability from 62% to 86% at day 14 while maintaining printability.
summary_en.validation: Cell viability assays and compressive modulus measurements validated the performance.
